paragraphs: Mentioned in Jerusalem Talmud Kilayim, chapter 1, halakhah 4, explaining adnei ha-sadeh: it is a “man of the mountain” that lives through its navel and dies when it is severed.[^1][^2]

notes.text: Supplied ייסא ערקא versus earlier audit יוסא עוקי and inherited provisional/uncertain scan status remain unadjudicated. Yisa Arka is transliteration, without an identity or added title. The headed person is the natural implicit explainer. בר נש דטור is the literal man-of-the-mountain description, not a modern biological claim.

1h 4 is the explicit Jerusalem Talmud locator without a new named check. The severed subject is unstated: navel/cord/connection or creature being cut off remain possibilities. Dies renders does-not-live contextually; no specific cord mechanism is invented.
